transcript.text: Hello, I'm here to help you get ready for your appointment. Could you tell me what has been bothering you?
I keep feeling light-headed and dizzy when I stand up, and it’s been worrying me.
Can you tell me a bit about when you first noticed this and how it came on, and also whether you have any allergies or bad reactions to medicines?
It came on a while back, not long after I started a new blood-pressure tablet. I don’t have any allergies to medicines that I know of.
How much does the dizziness affect what you can do during the day?
It’s been getting in the way a fair bit, and I’ve been cautious about going out because I worry about feeling faint.
Before this started, had you been diagnosed with any other long-term health conditions?
Yes, I’ve had high blood pressure for a long time, and I’ve got arthritis in both hips.
How strong would you say the light-headed or dizzy feeling usually is?
It’s enough to make me stop and hold on to something, but I couldn’t really put a number on it.
When you feel light-headed or dizzy, do you notice anything else happening at the same time?
No, I haven’t noticed chest pain, palpitations, blackouts, or weakness in my arms or legs.
When you feel light-headed or dizzy, where in your body do you notice that feeling most?
I’m not really sure — it’s just a swimmy, about-to-faint feeling rather than the room spinning.
How often do these swimmy, about-to-faint spells tend to happen?
It happens on and off through the day, mostly when I first get up.
Besides your blood pressure and arthritis, are there any other health conditions you see a doctor or nurse about regularly?
No, there aren’t any other long-term conditions I see them about regularly.
Since these swimmy spells started, have you noticed any changes in your appetite, sleep, weight or energy, or any changes in your bladder, bowels or breathing — or has none of that changed?
No, I haven’t noticed any changes in those.
When these light-headed spells first started, did they come on suddenly or gradually, or are you not sure?
It seemed to come on gradually rather than all at once.
Is there anything else you’ve noticed happening around the same time as these light-headed spells, even if it seems small or unrelated?
Not really, other than I’ve been more careful about going out because I’m worried about feeling faint.
Can you tell me about any medicines you take regularly, and whether any are new or have changed recently — and if you know, what dose you take?

I take a water tablet every morning, some painkillers for my hips, a small tablet for my stomach, and there’s a new blood-pressure tablet the nurse added a couple of weeks ago. I’m not sure of the doses offhand.
Do you remember if the new blood-pressure tablet was started before your light-headed spells began, after they began, or around the same time — or are you not sure?
I think the new tablet was started about a week before the dizziness began — the nurse added it a couple of weeks ago.
Thank you, that is very helpful. I have put together a short summary of what you told me. Please read it and tell me if anything should be corrected before it goes to your doctor.
